title: user_preferences.quiet_hours is unusable on an alembic-built database - the ORM cannot insert the row, and the consumer raises an uncaught TypeError

headline.defect: ORM declares String(5); migration 05_content_storage declares sa.Time(timezone=True); live column is timetz
headline.consequence: the ORM cannot insert a user_preferences row; the consumer's time.fromisoformat raises an uncaught TypeError
headline.fix: extend layer 05 (the project is pre-release, so the creating layer is corrected directly)
headline.verification: the ORM can insert the row, read back is str, consumer accepts, response model accepts

instrument.why_not_the_raw_driver: vthy's raw asyncpg read hid the jsonb defect
instrument.one_arm_per_process: the app engine is a module-level singleton

control_arm.note: test_db already existed (alembic-built), so create_all did not alter it; both arms measured the same schema

quiet_hours.writes: rejected (FK violations - sentinel users without FK drops)

the_discarded_attempt.why_discarded: the user reversed the design: extend the layer, not stack a revision; the project is pre-release
the_discarded_attempt.measured_defect: the 41-character revision id exceeded alembic's VARCHAR(32) alembic_version.version_num, causing the entire upgrade to roll back
the_discarded_attempt.user_quote: Why did you create a new file? I want you to edit its existing file.

the_user_reversal.rule: src/migrations/AGENTS.md: New schema changes should extend the relevant layer's upgrade()/downgrade() rather than stacking a new dated revision, unless the layer is already applied in production
the_user_reversal.reversal_condition: if layer 05 is ever applied in production, the rule reverses and a new revision is required

credential_id_hash.rationale: the read path looks a credential up BY that hash; a unique index permits unlimited NULLs

device_type.rationale: the ORM declares NOT NULL and the only writer always supplies one; the old nullable DB was the loose direction

measured: the fix works: the ORM can insert the row, read back is str, consumer accepts
the width rows are unchanged (auz2's scope)
explicitly_not_measured: no claim about production databases that already applied the old layer 05
no claim about the width rows' runtime impact (owned by auz2)

limits: The control arm measured the same database as the subject arm (test_db already existed); the before/after contrast comes from 9cmn's measurement vs this one.
The fix corrects layer 05's declaration; a database that already applied the old layer 05 keeps timetz until DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE + alembic upgrade head.
The user's reversal (extend the layer, not stack a revision) is recorded; if layer 05 is ever applied in production the rule reverses.
The width rows (files.storage_path, files.mime_type, audit_logs.user_agent, passkey_credentials.device_type) are measured but unchanged; they are auz2's scope.
